title: node 22.18 breaks npm package because of `experimental-strip-types` enabled
body:
### Version

v22.18.0

### Platform

```text
Linux / Windows / Azure devops build agents
```

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

After updating to node22.18 we see issues with builds. Looking through the change notes, I see that it now has enabled an experimental feature, and we now to have to add --no-experimental... to the command line in order to run our code in nodejs.

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

consistently failure in our CI pipelines unless --no-experimental-strip-types is added to node cli

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

minor releases should not add experimental features to an existing lts version

### What do you see instead?

Failing builds using node 22.18 (working fine with node 22.17)

### Additional information

_No response_

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
From what I can tell, the repro of @participant4 comes down to this:

1. The repro is using Mocha 10. That is prior to https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/pull/5366
2. The new type stripping support changes the error thrown from attempting to `import()` `some.spec.ts` from `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` to `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` (because it's using the `import readFile = promises.readFile` syntax not supported by type stripping, but this can be generalized to any TypeStript syntax not supported by type stripping)
3. Then this would be missed by the retrying logic in mocha https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/a908b3b86604d41d5751cccfaff505d7092c114f/lib/nodejs/esm-utils.js#L49-L51

I could fix it locally by adding `|| err.code === 'ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX'`  into the condition list mentioned in 3 in Mocha 10. Or I could fix it by simply upgrading to mocha 11 (which then would try `require()` first, and in that case, ts-node hooks would be applied first before Node.js handles them with type stripping). I don't know if Mocha would release patches for 10 again so the best course of action might be to just upgrade to mocha 11.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: I think the repro from  @participant4 is probably significantly different from what @participant3 or @reporter are seeing. In any case, the issues likely come from the module loading customizations in your dependencies not expecting Node.js to be able to handle TypeScript (but only with type stripping, without full transforms or tsconfig support). So it would be important to provide information/reproduction about what's in your dependencies that are customizing the module loading process (e.g. whether you use a testing framework like mocha or which version of it specifically, whether you use `ts-node/register`, `@swc-node/register`, `esbuild-register`, etc.)

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Tried reverting https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58657 and the issue persists.
I think the issue falls on the fact that we added the 'module-typescript' and 'commonjs-typescript' format to loaders.
This patch fixes it, I sent a PR to TSX https://github.com/privatenumber/tsx/pull/733:
```diff
marcoippolito@marcos-MacBook-Pro-3 tsx % git diff src/esm/hook/resolve.ts
diff --git a/src/esm/hook/resolve.ts b/src/esm/hook/resolve.ts
index 5c142f8..c6cb5db 100644
--- a/src/esm/hook/resolve.ts
+++ b/src/esm/hook/resolve.ts
@@ -336,6 +336,8 @@ let resolve: ResolveHook = async (
        // For TypeScript extensions that Node can't detect the format of
        if (
                !resolved.format
+               || resolved.format === 'commonjs-typescript'
+               || resolved.format === 'module-typescript'
                // Filter out data: (sourcemaps)
                && resolved.url.startsWith(fileUrlPrefix)
        ) {
```

comments.author: participant27
comments.body:
As others mentioned, I encountered issues with node >= 22.18  in combination with mocha. Additionally, we're using the `ts-node/esm` loader:

    $ mocha --require ts-node/esm

Setting `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-strip-types` fixed some of the issues, but caused others. Here's a minimised example to reproduce a bug that was introduced in 22.18.0 when used with `--no-experimental-strip-types`:

```
$ cat mocha-loader-bug.ts
import { config } from './config.js';

it('test', () => {
  const deployment = config.getRequired<string>('deployment');
  console.log('deployment:', deployment)
})
```
```
$ cat config.ts
export const config = {
  getRequired: <T>(key: string): T => key as T,
};
```
with `--no-experimental-strip-types`:
```
$ NODE_OPTIONS='--loader=ts-node/esm --no-experimental-strip-types' npx mocha mocha-loader-bug.ts
...
  1) test:
     ReferenceError: string is not defined
      at Context.<anonymous> (file://mocha-loader-bug.ts:4:41)
      at process.processImmediate (node:internal/timers:485:21)
```
without `--no-experimental-strip-types`:
```
$ NODE_OPTIONS='--loader=ts-node/esm' npx mocha mocha-loader-bug.ts

deployment: deployment
  ✔ test

  1 passing (2ms)
```
```
$ node --version
v22.18.0
$ npx mocha --version
11.7.2
$ npx ts-node --version
v10.9.2
